title: Control Systems
summary: Transfer functions, second-order response numbers (ζ, ω_n, overshoot, settling), steady-state error by system type, Routh–Hurwitz, Bode margins, root-locus rules, state space.
definitions: Laplace output/input with zero initial conditions.
Number of poles at the origin of G(s)H(s).
Highest power of s in the characteristic equation.
facts: Stable: all closed-loop poles in the left half-plane. Simple poles on jω axis → marginally stable.
Routh: number of sign changes in first column = number of RHP roots. Missing/negative coefficient → unstable.
Type 0: finite step error; Type 1: zero step error, finite ramp error; Type 2: zero ramp error.
Each pole: −20 dB/decade; each zero: +20 dB/decade.
Root locus starts at open-loop poles (K = 0), ends at zeros or infinity; symmetric about real axis; on real axis left of an odd count of poles+zeros.
Integral action removes steady-state error; derivative adds damping; lead improves transient/phase margin; lag improves steady state.
Negative feedback reduces gain, increases bandwidth, reduces sensitivity.
AC servomotor has high rotor resistance (linear, drooping torque–speed). Tachogenerator gives speed feedback; synchro pair is a position error detector.
traps: ω_n is √(constant term), not the constant term itself.
Gain margin is measured at the PHASE crossover frequency.
e_ss for a ramp uses K_v (multiply G by s first).

examples.q: s² + 4s + 16: find ω_n, ζ, M_p, t_s.
s³ + 2s² + 3s + K: range of K for stability.
